description: Phase 1 of provider-aware routing (P1c + P1e): a Grok stderr plan rate limit becomes IterationOutcome::RateLimit instead of a crash, and Grok session cleanup passes --session-id and deletes only that run's session directory. Later phases (P1b, P1a, P1d, P2, P4a, P3, P4b) get their own task files from the same PRD.

priorityPhilosophy.description: Hierarchy of what matters most when implementing tasks
hierarchy: 2. PHASE 2 FOUNDATION — typed signals and exact identifiers, no heuristics
3. FUNCTIONING CODE — sequential and wave map the same way
4. CORRECTNESS — red-first tests; idempotent, accurate results
5. CODE QUALITY — small local hunks, no dead code left behind
principles: Quality dimensions explicit — qualityDimensions on every implementation task
Edge cases live on the owning implementation task; tests are written and seen failing first
Scoped per-iteration tests; full suite at REVIEW-001, including pre-existing failures
Lean: the smallest change that is complete; delete heuristics rather than layering on them
Ship working code with tests; handle Option/Result explicitly; no unwrap() in production

prohibitedOutcomes: Classifying Grok's plan rate-limit message as Crash, Empty, or TransientBackend
Adding a bare 'rate limit' pattern, or narrowing or removing any existing is_rate_limited pattern
Appending a marker or the stderr text to RunnerResult.output to signal a limit (use a typed error)
Calling the Anthropic Usage API or the Claude probe because of a Grok limit
Keeping the before/after session-dir diff or pick_newest_by_mtime alongside --session-id
Deleting any ~/.grok/sessions entry other than the one UUID task-mgr passed
Running grok in a project root or touching existing ~/.grok/sessions directories while testing
Running cargo install or replacing the installed task-mgr binary
Tests that only assert no crash, or that call a live CLI or the live Usage API
Any per-task model field or top-level PRD model field

userStories.title: Clean up only the Grok session task-mgr created, via --session-id
userStories.description:
GrokRunner::spawn finds its session directory by diffing ~/.grok/sessions/<encoded cwd>/ before and after the run, and picks the newest by mtime when several appear (runner.rs ~:806-823, ~:952-970, pick_newest_by_mtime ~:471). An interactive Grok session started in the same cwd can be chosen and deleted by cleanup_session.

DO:
1. Red first: a runner test with a mock grok script that records argv, creates `<HOME>/.grok/sessions/<encoded cwd>/<uuid from --session-id>` and, during the run, a second newer `<other-uuid>` directory (the interactive session), plus prompt_history.jsonl. Assert argv contains `--session-id <uuid>`, RunnerResult.session_id == that uuid, and after dispatch cleanup the other directory and prompt_history.jsonl still exist. Paste the failing output first.
2. Generate Uuid::new_v4() per spawn, push `--session-id <uuid>` before `--prompt-file`, and return Some(uuid), mirroring Claude (runner.rs ~:601-603).
3. Delete the pre/post snapshot, pick_newest_by_mtime, and the dir-diff test (replace it with the new test). Update the WORKAROUND(grok-cli-no-persistence-off) comment.

Use a temp HOME in tests. Never touch the real ~/.grok.

E8: argv carries --session-id <uuid>; RunnerResult.session_id is that uuid; the concurrent other-uuid directory and prompt_history.jsonl survive cleanup
E9: grok exits before creating its directory → cleanup returns Ok and prints no cleanup warning
E10: HOME unset → no cleanup, no panic
Cleanup called twice for the same uuid returns Ok both times

invariants: cleanup_session removes at most <encoded cwd>/<uuid task-mgr generated>
